scenarios.name: Hero Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays product name, tagline, and value proposition prominently (REQ-1, REQ-2)

steps.description: Navigate to the MirDB landing page URL
steps.context: User arrives at landing page from search engine, GitHub link, or direct URL

steps.description: Check that the hero section contains product name 'MirDB', tagline, and brief description
steps.context: Hero section should be the first visible element on page load

steps.description: Confirm primary call-to-action button is present and functional
steps.context: CTA should link to getting started or GitHub repository

test_cases.expected: Product name 'MirDB' is displayed prominently in h1 or similar heading element
Tagline 'Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol' or equivalent is visible
Primary CTA button (e.g., 'Get Started' or 'View on GitHub') is present and clickable
Brief description explaining Memcached compatibility with persistent storage is displayed

scenarios.name: Features Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify key features section highlighting LSM tree architecture, Memcached protocol support, and persistence (REQ-3)

steps.description: Scroll or navigate to the features section of the landing page
steps.context: Features section should be easily accessible from hero section

steps.description: Check that all key features are presented in visual cards or blocks
steps.context: Each feature should have a clear title and description

test_cases.expected: Feature card/block describing drop-in replacement for existing memcached clients is present
Feature card/block describing data survival using SSTable-based storage is present

test_cases.input: Check for LSM Tree Architecture feature
test_cases.expected: Feature card/block describing efficient write performance with background compaction is present
Feature card/block describing Tokio-based async I/O is present
Features section uses proper semantic HTML elements (section, article, heading hierarchy)

scenarios.name: Getting Started Section
scenarios.description: Verify getting started section with basic usage example and installation instructions (REQ-4, REQ-8)

steps.description: Scroll or navigate to the getting started section
steps.context: Section should guide users on how to begin using MirDB

steps.description: Check that code examples are properly formatted and readable
steps.context: Code should show server startup and basic memcached commands

test_cases.expected: Code example showing 'mirdb -c /path/to/config.toml' or similar startup command is present
Example showing how to connect with memcached client (e.g., telnet localhost 12333) is present
Code examples demonstrate basic SET and GET operations with expected output
Code blocks have proper syntax highlighting or monospace formatting for readability
Clear instructions on how to install or build MirDB are present

scenarios.name: Supported Commands Display
scenarios.description: Verify supported commands section displays available memcached commands (REQ-5)

steps.description: Locate the section displaying supported commands
steps.context: Section may be part of technical details or separate

steps.description: Check that all supported commands are listed with descriptions
steps.context: Commands include storage, retrieval, deletion, and MirDB-specific

test_cases.expected: SET, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND commands are listed
GET, GETS commands are listed
DELETE command is listed
INFO and MAJOR_COMPACTION commands are listed

scenarios.name: Default Configuration Display
scenarios.description: Verify default configuration parameters are displayed (REQ-6)

steps.description: Locate the section displaying default configuration
steps.context: May be part of technical details section

steps.description: Check that default configuration parameters are accurately displayed
steps.context: Values should match actual MirDB defaults

test_cases.expected: Default listen address '0.0.0.0:12333' is displayed
Max LSM levels '7' is displayed
Default work directory '/tmp/mirdb' is displayed
SSTable max size '100MB' is displayed
Memtable max size '4MB' is displayed

scenarios.name: Navigation Links
scenarios.description: Verify navigation links to documentation, GitHub repository, and community resources (REQ-7)

steps.description: Locate all navigation links in header, footer, and body
steps.context: Links should be clearly visible and accessible

steps.description: Check that all links point to correct destinations
steps.context: Links should not be broken or point to placeholder URLs

test_cases.expected: Link to MirDB GitHub repository is present and valid
Link to documentation is present (may be to GitHub README or docs site)
Footer contains links to GitHub, license information, and other relevant resources

test_cases.input: Verify external links open in new tab
test_cases.expected: External links have target='_blank' and rel='noopener noreferrer' attributes

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Desktop
scenarios.description: Verify page renders correctly on desktop devices (NFR-1)

steps.description: Open page in browser with desktop viewport (1920x1080, 1366x768)
steps.context: Standard desktop screen sizes

steps.description: Check that all content is properly laid out and readable
steps.context: No horizontal scrolling, proper content width

test_cases.expected: Page renders correctly without horizontal scrolling, content is centered and readable
Page renders correctly at smaller desktop resolution
Feature cards display in grid or row layout appropriate for desktop
Navigation links are visible without hamburger menu on desktop

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Tablet
scenarios.description: Verify page renders correctly on tablet devices (NFR-1)

steps.description: Open page with tablet viewport (768x1024, 1024x768)
steps.context: Standard tablet screen sizes in portrait and landscape

steps.description: Check that layout adapts appropriately for tablet size
steps.context: Content should reflow for medium screens

test_cases.expected: Page adapts to tablet portrait mode with appropriate layout
Page adapts to tablet landscape mode with appropriate layout
Feature cards reflow to 2-column or stacked layout as appropriate

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Mobile
scenarios.description: Verify page renders correctly on mobile devices (NFR-1)

steps.description: Open page with mobile viewport (375x667, 414x896)
steps.context: Common iPhone and Android screen sizes

steps.description: Check that layout is optimized for mobile viewing
steps.context: Single column layout, touch-friendly elements

test_cases.expected: Page renders in single-column layout, all content readable

test_cases.input: Load page at 414x896 viewport (iPhone 11 Pro Max)
test_cases.expected: Page renders correctly on larger mobile screen

scenarios.name: Page Load Performance
scenarios.description: Verify page loads within 3 seconds on standard broadband connection (NFR-2)

steps.description: Use performance tools to measure initial page load
steps.context: Simulated broadband connection (10+ Mbps)

steps.description: Check CSS, JS, and image loading times
steps.context: Identify any blocking resources

test_cases.expected: DOMContentLoaded event fires within 2 seconds
Full page load completes within 3 seconds
Total page size (HTML, CSS, JS, images) is under 500KB
CSS is minimal and JS is deferred or async where possible

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Semantic HTML
scenarios.description: Verify page uses proper semantic HTML and heading hierarchy (NFR-3)

steps.description: Review HTML for semantic elements and proper structure
steps.context: Page should use HTML5 semantic elements

steps.description: Check that headings follow proper h1-h6 order
steps.context: No skipped heading levels

test_cases.expected: Page contains exactly one h1 element (product name)
Headings follow logical order (h1 > h2 > h3) without skipping levels
Page uses header, main, nav, section, article, footer elements appropriately
Page has proper landmark regions (banner, main, navigation, contentinfo)

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Color Contrast
scenarios.description: Verify sufficient color contrast ratios for text readability (NFR-3)

steps.description: Check foreground/background color combinations
steps.context: WCAG 2.1 AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text

test_cases.expected: Body text has minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio with background
Large headings have minimum 3:1 contrast ratio
Links are distinguishable from surrounding text (color + underline or 3:1 contrast)
Button text has sufficient contrast with button background

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Keyboard Navigation

steps.context: Focus should be clearly visible

test_cases.expected: All interactive elements (links, buttons) are reachable via Tab key
Focused elements have visible outline or indicator
Tab order follows visual/logical order of content
Skip to main content link is present and functional

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Screen Reader
scenarios.description: Verify page content is accessible to screen readers (NFR-3)

steps.description: Check that all images have appropriate alt attributes

steps.context: Don't overuse ARIA when native HTML suffices

test_cases.expected: All images have alt attributes (descriptive or empty for decorative)
Links have descriptive text or aria-label indicating destination
Code examples are readable by screen readers with appropriate markup
